knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Unvalidated caller-provided tensor geometry causes out-of-bounds memory access during view/copy materialization
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Operators that accept explicit size and stride metadata may trust that metadata to be consistent with the backing storage; when invoked with invalid geometry, downstream materialization can read or write outside allocated memory.

risk_dimensions.shape: Small logical shapes combined with custom size lists; size/stride mismatches
risk_dimensions.dtype: Integer dtypes such as int64 that produce wide memory accesses
risk_dimensions.memory: Small backing storage with stride values that exceed allocation; non-contiguous, zero, or negative stride layouts
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Direct operator invocation with caller-provided size/stride before materialization or copy

failure_mechanism.description: The operator accepts caller-provided size and stride metadata without validating source storage bounds; downstream copy or materialization uses the resulting invalid geometry, causing out-of-bounds access at the kernel layer.

input_exploration: Explore size and stride combinations whose computed logical extents exceed the allocated backing storage
Mutate stride metadata across large, zero, negative, and sparse values
Construct tensors with small storage and custom size/stride mismatches
Force materialization of views or copies created from custom geometry
constraint_awareness: Stride-accepting operators may assume tensor geometry is consistent with storage allocation
Caller-provided metadata can bypass high-level tensor validation paths
Memory safety failures may only appear during actual materialization rather than metadata construction
oracle_strategy: Run under AddressSanitizer or comparable memory error detector
Monitor for heap-buffer-overflow, invalid reads, or process crashes during materialization

transferability.reason: The risk applies broadly to APIs that accept explicit size/stride metadata, view/copy operators, and kernels that materialize tensor geometry without independently validating storage bounds.

important_considerations: Inspect APIs that accept explicit size, stride, or storage offset metadata and then materialize or copy tensor data
Test small backing storage with inconsistent geometry to expose missing bounds checks
Consider both API and kernel layer validation gaps when generating inputs
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that create tensors with minimal storage and custom size/stride metadata, feed them to stride-accepting APIs, force materialization, and run under a memory sanitizer to detect invalid access.
